response.sql: WITH filtered AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, t.bandusagepct, o.observstation, o.weathprofile FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.pointaccarc > 4.86), grouped AS (SELECT observstation, weathprofile, AVG(bandusagepct) AS group_avg_band, COUNT(telescregistry) AS group_count FROM filtered GROUP BY observstation, weathprofile) SELECT AVG(group_avg_band) AS avg_of_group_avg_band, AVG(group_count) AS avg_group_count FROM grouped;

assumptions.assumption: "High side of a 4.86 cutoff" means pointaccarc strictly greater than 4.86, so a telescope at exactly 4.86 is excluded.
Telescopes with a NULL weathprofile form their own group rather than being dropped, since GROUP BY treats NULL as a distinct value. The request does not say how to handle missing weather profiles.

The group count is the number of telescopes in the group, counted whether or not their bandusagepct is NULL. Groups whose bandusagepct values are all NULL have a NULL average and are skipped by the outer AVG, as the request asks.
The average of group counts includes every group, since COUNT never returns NULL.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude telescopes whose observatory has a NULL weathprofile, so only groups with a real weather profile are averaged.
alternatives.sql: WITH filtered AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, t.bandusagepct, o.observstation, o.weathprofile FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.pointaccarc > 4.86 AND o.weathprofile IS NOT NULL), grouped AS (SELECT observstation, weathprofile, AVG(bandusagepct) AS group_avg_band, COUNT(telescregistry) AS group_count FROM filtered GROUP BY observstation, weathprofile) SELECT AVG(group_avg_band) AS avg_of_group_avg_band, AVG(group_count) AS avg_group_count FROM grouped;
